OTP_DEV_PREVIEW_ENABLED.title: OTP dev preview is on
OTP_DEV_PREVIEW_ENABLED.fix: OTP codes are returned by the API and written to logs, so anyone can pass email verification and 2FA. Set APP_AUTH_OTP_DEV_PREVIEW=false on the server and restart the backend.

COOKIE_SAMESITE_NONE_INSECURE.title: SameSite=None cookie without Secure
COOKIE_SAMESITE_NONE_INSECURE.fix: Browsers will reject the session cookie. Set APP_COOKIE_SECURE=true (requires HTTPS) or change APP_COOKIE_SAME_SITE back to Lax.

COOKIE_NOT_SECURE.title: Session cookie is not marked Secure
COOKIE_NOT_SECURE.fix: The sign-in cookie can travel over unencrypted HTTP. On a real server set APP_COOKIE_SECURE=true.

CORS_WILDCARD.title: CORS allows any origin (*)
CORS_WILDCARD.fix: Any website could call the API with a user's session. List the exact frontend domains in APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

CORS_LOCALHOST.title: CORS still allows localhost
CORS_LOCALHOST.fix: Localhost origins are for development only. Remove them from APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS on a real server.

CORS_PLAIN_HTTP.title: CORS allows an unencrypted HTTP origin
CORS_PLAIN_HTTP.fix: Allow only https:// origins in APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

MAIL_DISABLED.title: Email sending is off
MAIL_DISABLED.fix: OTP emails (account verification, email 2FA, password reset) are not delivered. Configure SMTP and set APP_MAIL_ENABLED=true.

ACCESS_TOKEN_LONG_LIVED.title: Access tokens live longer than 24 hours
ACCESS_TOKEN_LONG_LIVED.fix: A leaked token stays usable for a long time. Lower APP_JWT_EXPIRATION_MS (for example 15–60 minutes); the refresh token keeps users signed in.

REFRESH_TOKEN_LONG_LIVED.title: Refresh tokens live longer than 30 days
REFRESH_TOKEN_LONG_LIVED.fix: Consider lowering app.jwt.refresh-expiration-ms so old sessions expire sooner.

NOT_PRODUCTION_PROFILE.title: Not recognised as a production deployment
NOT_PRODUCTION_PROFILE.fix: No prod profile, no cookie domain and no public https CORS origin. If this is a real server, review deploy/.env.production.

SECRET_MISSING.title: A required secret is missing
SECRET_MISSING.fix: Set a long random value in deploy/.env.production and restart the service.

SECRET_KNOWN_DEFAULT.title: A secret uses a default or example value
SECRET_KNOWN_DEFAULT.fix: This value appears in source code or example files, so treat it as leaked. Replace it with a new random value now.

SECRET_TOO_SHORT.title: A secret is shorter than the minimum
SECRET_TOO_SHORT.fix: Generate a longer value, for example: openssl rand -base64 48.

revokeAll.title: Sign out all users
revokeAll.description: Revokes every session (refresh and access tokens) of every account except yours. Use it after a suspected breach or a key change.

sessions.mechanism: Revocation is immediate: the refresh token is invalidated and every access token issued before that moment is rejected. Users just sign in again.
sessions.selfWarning: This is your account: you will be signed out.

confirm.revokeUser: Revoke all sessions of {name}? They will be signed out on every device.
confirm.revokeSelf: This is your own account. Revoking signs you out immediately on every device, including this one. Continue?
confirm.revokeAll: Sign out ALL other users on every device? This cannot be undone; your own session is kept.
confirm.reset2fa: Turn off two-factor authentication for {name} and remove their authenticator key? Only do this after verifying the user's identity (for example a lost phone).
confirm.reset2faRevoke: Also sign {name} out on every device? (Recommended: OK. Choose Cancel to keep existing sessions.)

done.REVOKE_ALL_SESSIONS: Signed out {count} accounts ({tokens} refresh tokens revoked).
done.RESET_2FA: 2FA reset. The user can sign in with their password and turn 2FA on again.
done.selfSignedOut: Your own session was revoked; you will be taken to the sign-in page.

sessions.footnote: Each account has at most one refresh session; signing in on a new device replaces the old one. Every action is written to the audit log.

policy.readOnlyNote: Read-only values from the running server configuration. To change them, edit deploy/.env.production on the VPS and restart the backend.
policy.allGood: No issues found in the sign-in configuration.

notice.title: Secrets are never shown or edited on the web
notice.body: This page only reports whether each secret is set, long enough and not a default; values are never displayed. Secrets are managed in deploy/.env.production on the VPS.

notes.DERIVED_FROM_JWT_SECRET: Not set: derived from the JWT signing key.
notes.REQUIRED_WHEN_BILLING_PROVIDER_ENABLED: Required only when the payment provider is enabled.
notes.REQUIRED_WHEN_SMTP_AUTH_ENABLED: Required only when email with SMTP authentication is enabled.

aiKey.title: AI provider API key
aiKey.missing: Not configured. The AI assistant will not work.

rotation.title: Secret rotation guide
rotation.general: On the VPS: edit deploy/.env.production, re-run docker compose to restart the services, then check System health. Generate new values with: openssl rand -base64 48.

jwt.title: JWT signing key (APP_JWT_SECRET)
jwt.body: Changing it ends every session and users must sign in again. If APP_AI_ROUTER_SECRET is not set, the AI key is derived from the JWT key, so re-enter the AI API key afterwards.

billingIpn.title: IPN secret (APP_BILLING_IPN_SECRET)
billingIpn.body: Update it at the payment provider and on the server at the same time, otherwise payment notifications are rejected.

aiRouter.title: AI router encryption key (APP_AI_ROUTER_SECRET)
aiRouter.body: Changing it makes the stored AI API key unreadable; re-enter the API key on the AI Router page after restarting.

storage.title: Storage keys (APP_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY / APP_STORAGE_SECRET_KEY)
storage.body: Create a new key pair in MinIO/R2/S3, update the server, confirm uploads work, then delete the old pair.

mail.title: SMTP password (SMTP_PASSWORD)
mail.body: Change it at the email provider, update the server, then send a password-reset OTP to test.

database.title: Database password (POSTGRES_PASSWORD)
database.body: Change the user's password in PostgreSQL (ALTER USER) first, then update the server and restart the backend. POSTGRES_PASSWORD only applies when the database is first created.
